question: The Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1972 came into effect from the 1st April, 1972.
The Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1972 shall also apply to members of all India Services.
'Minor' means a person who has not completed the age of eighteen years.
The Appointing Authority may authorise to withdrawal of pension if the pensioner is convicted of a serious crime.
A Group 'A' officer is required to obtain the previous sanction of the Government for acceptance of any commercial employment before the expiry of six months from the date of retirement.

The service rendered by a state Government servant shall qualify for the period to be accounted for under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1972 if he is transferred to the Government of India.
Half of the service paid from contingencies before absorption in regular employment counts for qualifying service if there is no break in service.

The period which a Government servant is put under suspension shall not count as qualifying service even if he has been fully exonerated as the Government servant does not perform any duty during suspension.
The dismissal of a Government servant from a service entails forfeiture of his past service.
A Government servant must not retire on the due date of retirement unless a Competent Authority issues an office order to that effect.
Leave cannot be claimed as of right.
A Government servant on extraordinary leave is not entitled to any leave salary.
Casual leave and Special Casual Leave can also be combined with other kinds of leave.
Leave may also be granted to a Government servant under suspension.
Maternity leave cannot be granted in the case of threatened abortion.
Joining time cannot be combined with any regular leave.
No joining time is admissible if the transfer is within the same station.
Joining time commences from the date of relinquishment of charge of the old post if the charge is made over in the forenoon.
The CCS (Joining Time) Rules, 1979 shall also apply to Government servants who are paid out of contingencies.
Unavailed Joining Time shall be credited to the leave account of a Government servant as earned leave.

The joining time admissible to a Government servant on transfer is 12 days when the distance between the old and new headquarters is less than 1000 kms but the journey necessarily involves more than 200 kms by road.
